rv.q: If this stuff rings your intellectual bell, “Solaris” (which is based on the 1961 novel by the Polish scribe Stanislaw Lem) is your show.
Full of delightfully manic oceanic peaks and long esoteric stretches of calm, the play delves into the seduction of the past and explores duality and memory.
This is one of the most astounding, thought-provoking and beautifully produced plays in Griffin Theatre’s long history of fine productions.
But without big names or budget, director Scott Weinstein and his all-in cast have delivered a taut, smart production that succeeds dramatically, visually and thematically.
"Solaris" is an essential story in our futuristic world of personalized operating systems and hyper-realistic video games.
The result is a thoughtful exploration of human identity and the possibility (or not) of truly knowing someone else.
I will say this about this play 'it is worth catching, even if you are not a sci-fi fan'.

cn.t: Critics praise this North American premiere as a riveting sci-fi thriller that translates surprisingly well to the intimate stage, though the cerebral exploration of consciousness and alien intelligence proves more thought-provoking than dramatic.
